title: Monitors of every agent's model requests under fixed rules, and the stations of the bug loop
request: The owner asked for monitoring that helps find bugs and track the agents and models over time.
spec: Per agent purpose over recent days: requests, failures with an interval, median and high-percentile delay, tokens and euro, marked red or amber by rules fixed in code; and how many flagged sessions are candidates, waiting, accepted, rejected and replayed as regression cases.
plan: read the usage log through its own interface
the per-purpose numbers and the fixed rules
count the bug loop's stations from the existing files
the command, the route and the panel

decisions.decision: Rules fixed in code before any reading, with a minimum of requests for red
decisions.why: a red mark on three requests would be noise; a rule moved after a reading would be no rule

decisions.decision: Reuse the existing candidates, reviews and regression replay instead of a new loop
decisions.why: the pieces existed; what was missing was seeing where each case stands

change: dclab_rnd/bench/monitors.py (new), bench/__main__.py (monitors), agentic/pages/bench.py and accounts/guard.py (the owner-only route), views/admin.html (the panel), the generated app, docs/guides/BENCHMARK.md, tests/test_bench_monitors.py.

findings.defect: The bug loop had no candidates
findings.scenario: the first reading of the workspace counted no flagged session as a candidate
findings.cause: the candidates are built by make datasets, which had not run on the current records
findings.fix: not a code fix: the panel names the command that builds them

findings.defect: Every page load read the whole recent log with its prompt texts
findings.scenario: on PostgreSQL each load could move many prompt texts and silently undercount past its limit
findings.cause: the monitors read the recent rows whole and filtered them afterwards
findings.fix: the usage logs read only the window, without the prompt column, and the summary says when it was cut

measurements.name: the first reading of the workspace's last days
measurements.result: the lead agent marked amber for its daily spend; the campaign marked amber for slow requests; Home's failures under the red line
limits: the usage log of one workspace on one machine

outcome: The owner sees which agent fails, slows or spends too much, and where each flagged session stands on its way to a regression test.
lessons: a loop that exists in pieces is invisible until someone counts its stations
risks: the rules' thresholds are a first choice; a change must be a new rule, written before the next reading
